description: A Go ok package line counts as one passed test only when no --- PASS or --- FAIL line for that package was read before it, so a run with -v counts each test once.

specs.description: A -v run of one passing test is one test
specs.given:
output "=== RUN   TestX
--- PASS: TestX (0.00s)
PASS
ok  	demo/pkg	0.01s
" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: A -v run of N passing tests in one package is N
specs.given: output with three lines "--- PASS: TestA (0.00s)", "--- PASS: TestB (0.00s)" and "--- PASS: TestC (0.00s)", then "PASS" and "ok  \tdemo/pkg\t0.02s", from a run that exited 0

specs.description: A run without -v is counted as before: the package line is one test
specs.given: output "ok  \tdemo/pkg\t0.01s\n" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: The tab-only form of the package line follows the same rule
specs.given: output "--- PASS: TestX (0.00s)\nok\tdemo/pkg\t0.01s\n" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: A sealed Go test bound to a verbose configured runner is judged as one passing test
specs.given:
a configured runner whose run of one passing test exits 0 and prints "=== RUN   TestX
--- PASS: TestX (0.00s)
PASS
ok  	demo/pkg	0.01s
"

specs.description: Each package is judged on its own lines since the previous package line
specs.given:
output "--- PASS: TestA
--- PASS: TestB
ok  	demo/p1	0.01s
ok  	demo/p2	0.01s
" from a run that exited 0, where p1 listed two tests and p2 listed none

specs.description: Two verbose packages each count only their listed tests
specs.given:
output "--- PASS: TestA
ok  	demo/p1	0.01s
--- PASS: TestB
ok  	demo/p2	0.01s
" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: The package line of a verbose run is not counted as another test
specs.given: output "--- PASS: TestX (0.00s)\nok  \tdemo/pkg\t0.01s\n" from a run that exited 0
specs.then: it does not return Evidence::Passed { tests: 2 }

specs.description: A verbose run of one correct test is not refused as matching two tests
specs.given:
a configured runner whose run exits 0 and prints "--- PASS: TestX (0.00s)
PASS
ok  	demo/pkg	0.01s
"
specs.then: it does not return Verdict::Ambiguous(2), or any Verdict::Ambiguous

specs.description: Lines listed for one package do not stop a later unlisted package line from counting
specs.given:
output "--- PASS: TestA
ok  	demo/p1	0.01s
ok  	demo/p2	0.01s
" from a run that exited 0
specs.then: it does not return Evidence::Passed { tests: 1 }; it returns Evidence::Passed { tests: 2 }

specs.description: Over all sequences of passing Go packages, each listed test counts once and each unlisted package line counts once
specs.given: any sequence of packages, each printing k ≥ 0 lines "--- PASS: T…" followed by its "ok  \t<pkg>\t<t>s" line, from a run that exited 0, with at least one package
specs.then: it returns Evidence::Passed { tests: Σ over packages of (k if k > 0 else 1) }

specs.description: A Go package without test files is still recognised with no tests
specs.given: output "?   \tdemo/internal/ports\t[no test files]\n" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: A Go run that matched no test is still vacuous
specs.given: output "ok  \tdemo/pkg\t0.01s [no tests to run]\n" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: Other runners' output is read as before
specs.given: cargo output "running 3 tests\ntest result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed\n" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: A failed verbose Go test still fails the run
specs.given:
output "--- FAIL: TestX (0.00s)
FAIL
FAIL	demo/pkg	0.01s
"
specs.then: it returns Evidence::Failed and never Evidence::Passed

specs.description: A failure in one package is not hidden by a passing package line elsewhere
specs.given:
output "--- FAIL: TestA
FAIL	demo/p1	0.01s
--- PASS: TestB
ok  	demo/p2	0.01s
" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: A run that exited non-zero is not passed by any Go lines
specs.given: output "--- PASS: TestX\nok  \tdemo/pkg\t0.01s\n" from a run that exited non-zero
specs.then: it returns Evidence::Failed { reason: "the gate exited non-zero" }

specs.description: A zero-test marker line is not counted as a test
specs.given: output "?   \tdemo/p1\t[no test files]\nok  \tdemo/p2\t0.01s\n" from a run that exited 0

specs.description: Over all Go outputs, any failure line fails the run whether or not it is verbose
specs.given: any output from a run that exited 0 that contains at least one line starting "--- FAIL", a line "FAIL", or a line starting "FAIL\t", in any position among any "--- PASS" and ok package lines

specs.description: Over all outputs with no Go ok package line, the count is the same as the count of the --- PASS and other runners' lines
specs.given: any output from a run that exited 0 that contains no line starting "ok  \t" or "ok\t" and no failure lines
specs.then: its result equals the result for the same output read under the reading rules in force before this ADR

specs.description: A test with passing subtests is one test
specs.given: A go test -v run of one test TestS03 with two t.Run subtests, printing --- PASS: TestS03/fixture, --- PASS: TestS03/real_tree, --- PASS: TestS03 and the ok package line

specs.description: A failing subtest still fails the run
specs.given: A go test -v run of one test whose subtest fails: --- FAIL: TestS03/fixture, --- FAIL: TestS03, FAIL pkg

specs.description: Subtest lines never add to the count
specs.given: Any go test -v output of passing tests in one package, where each top-level test may have any number of passing t.Run subtests
specs.then: It is Passed with tests equal to the number of top-level --- PASS lines (names without a /)
